title: [Chapitre] IV. Analysis situs (première mouture) : notes manuscrites (10/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from pp. 45-46): M is a set of 'cells' or 'simplices' with a face preorder ≤. A 'figure' is a subset F of M of a certain admissible kind, abstracting a finite simplicial or polyhedral complex. F_X denotes the figure generated by X, the closure of X under ≤. Figures are ≤-closed. Two figures are compatible if their union is again a figure. A ≤-closed part of a figure is a 'sous-figure' (subfigure). Underlying all this is a primitive notion of subdivision F' of a figure F. Grothendieck is building an axiomatic, combinatorial 'analysis situs' (tame/PL topology), in the spirit of the 'topologie modérée' of Esquisse d'un programme.

Page 47:
(1) Definition. G is a refinement of F, written F ≪ G, if there is a subdivision F' of F with G ⊂ F' (G a subfigure of F'). Geometrically, G is a subcomplex of some subdivision of F, so |G| ⊂ |F| and G is 'finer'. He wants ≪ to be an order relation.
(2) C4. Let G be a subfigure of a figure F and G' a subdivision of G.
- First attempt: G' ∪ (F∖G) is a subdivision of F, the union being disjoint (boxed: G'∩F ⊂ G, hence G'∩F = G'∩G).
- He then corrects this ('Corriger'). The corrected statement is: there exists a subdivision of F inducing G' on G. Equivalently, every subdivision of a subfigure is induced by a subdivision of the whole figure (the struck 'Cor. 1', marked OK).
- The margin notes that this is proved in the topological literature on triangulations.
(3) Cor 2. ≪ is an order relation. Transitivity follows from C4 plus the fact that a subdivision of a subdivision is a subdivision. Reflexivity is trivial.
(4) A struck draft proposition starts to characterize X ∈ F through compatibility of X with F together with F_X refining F. It is restated cleanly on p.48 as Cor. 3: G ⊂ F iff G is compatible with F and G ≪ F. Hence X ≤ Y iff X, Y are compatible and X ≪ Y. In other words, the face order is recovered from the compatibility and refinement relations.
errors: The first form of C4 is false in a genuine PL/simplicial setting. G' ∪ (F∖G) is not in general a subdivision of F, nor even a complex, because cells of F∖G with faces in G must also be subdivided. Grothendieck himself flags this ('Corriger') and replaces it with the correct existence statement: some subdivision of F induces G'.

Cor 2 (≪ is an order) has a gap on antisymmetry. From G ⊂ F' and F ⊂ G'' one needs that a figure contained as a subfigure in a subdivision of itself (same support) equals that subdivision. This needs an extra axiom, e.g. finiteness/counting or 'support' arguments, not visible on this page. Without it, ≪ is only a preorder.

C4 in the corrected form is itself a nontrivial theorem in PL topology (extension of subdivisions). In an axiomatic framework it must be taken as an axiom on the subdivision notion; it is not derived from the stated axioms.

ideas.what: Refinement relation F ≪ G: G is a subfigure of some subdivision of F
ideas.modern_name: Subcomplex of a subdivision; the refinement preorder on PL polyhedra / triangulations
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical PL topology (Alexander, Whitehead, Zeeman; Rourke–Sanderson)
ideas.where_published: Only the general programme of 'topologie modérée' in Esquisse d'un programme (1984); no such formal development published

ideas.what: Every subdivision of a subcomplex extends to a subdivision of the whole complex (C4 / Cor.1)
ideas.modern_name: Extension of subdivisions lemma (via derived subdivisions)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard PL topology (J.H.C. Whitehead, Zeeman, Rourke–Sanderson)

ideas.what: Membership and face order recovered from compatibility plus refinement: X ∈ F iff X compatible with F and X ≪ F (developed on p.48)
ideas.modern_name: Characterization of the subcomplex relation in an axiomatic cell/figure calculus

ideas.what: Axiomatic combinatorial 'analysis situs' via a set of cells, figures and subdivisions
ideas.modern_name: Axiomatic tame topology / PL categories; o-minimal-type foundations
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck's programme (Esquisse); later o-minimality (van den Dries, Pillay–Steinhorn, Knight)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5 announces tame topology but not these axioms

missed.claim: Part of an unpublished axiomatization of PL/tame topology. Figures in a poset of cells are equipped with an abstract subdivision relation, and the extension-of-subdivisions property and the refinement order are isolated as basic axioms or lemmas. The page itself is routine, but the framework as a whole remains undocumented in the literature.
missed.quote: On veut que ce soit une relation d'ordre ... toute subdivision de G est induite par une subdivision de F OK
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Of modest interest as evidence of how Grothendieck intended to found 'topologie modérée' combinatorially. It could be compared with o-minimal and semi-algebraic triangulation axiomatics. No new theorem appears here.

deep.surprise_reason: The content is standard PL topology (refinement, extension of subdivisions) recast axiomatically. Grothendieck even notes it is known in the topological literature. The interest is only documentary, as part of the unpublished 1986 tame-topology foundations.
transcription_corrections: 'et le simplexe est disparu' should read approximately 'et la réunion est disjointe' (referring to G' ∪ (F∖G)).
'(i.e. G figure de G(F))' is more likely '(i.e. G figure, G ⊂ F)'.
Left margin near the definition reads 'On écrit F ≪ G', with the arrow symbol ≪, not ⇐.

The marginal note 'C'est démontré dans les travaux topologiques et plus' is mostly illegible. It seems to refer to proofs in the topological literature (on triangulations/subdivisions); the exact words are uncertain.
The bottom struck block is the draft of what becomes Cor. 3 on p.48 (X ∈ F iff X compatible with F and X ≪ F), not a separate proposition.
